title: Hyderabad Police Book Husband and Three Friends After Myanmar Woman Says She Was Locked In and Raped
excerpt: An 18-year-old woman from Myanmar told police her husband locked her inside their rented Hyderabad home and sent three friends to sexually assault her; an FIR for rape, wrongful confinement and criminal intimidation was registered on October 26.
body:
• An 18-year-old woman from Myanmar has alleged that her husband locked her inside their rented home in Hyderabad and sent three of his friends to sexually assault her, threatening to kill her if she told anyone.
  • The alleged assaults came to light on October 23, when the landlord came to collect rent, found the house locked from outside and broke the lock open.
  • On October 26 a relative took her to a police station; an FIR has been registered against her husband and the three men for rape, wrongful confinement and criminal intimidation.
  • If you or someone you know in India faces violence at home, call 112 for emergency help or 181, the women helpline.

An 18-year-old woman from Myanmar has told Hyderabad police that her husband locked her inside their rented house and sent three of his friends to rape her. The allegations, set out in her complaint, name her husband Mohammad Fayaz and three men — Ahmad Mujeeb, Noor Kamal and Zia-ur-Rehman — and an FIR has been registered on charges of rape, wrongful confinement and criminal intimidation, according to The Daily Jagran. The accused have not been convicted; these are allegations under investigation.

What the complaint says

"The accused have not been convicted; these are allegations under investigation."

The woman, identified in reports as Humaira Tamanna, said she had been living in Cox's Bazar, Bangladesh, when she met Fayaz. After their marriage he brought her to Hyderabad — one account dates the move to May last year — and they lived in a rented apartment. She alleged that Fayaz brought the three friends to live in the home, would leave after locking the house from outside, and sent his friends inside, during which they sexually assaulted her. Two of them threatened to kill her if she disclosed the assaults, she said, and fear kept her from reporting them, according to PublicNext.

https://x.com/IndiaToday/status/2114979120983728244

How it came to light

The ordeal surfaced on October 23, when the house owner came to collect pending rent and found the house locked from outside. He broke open the lock, allowing the woman to leave. She contacted her family using another person's mobile phone and was taken to a relative's house. On October 26, her relative — named in reports as Mohammad Rasheed — took her to a police station, where she lodged her complaint.

That sequence is the part of this story that generalises: the survivor had no phone of her own to call from, no key to leave by, and no local support until a landlord's rent visit and a relative's intervention broke the isolation. Police have registered the case; the investigation, and any arrests and medical and forensic evidence, will determine what happens next. Readers should treat the details above as the complainant's account as reported, not as findings of a court.

Help is available in India around the clock: dial 112 in an emergency, or 181, the national women helpline, for support and referral.
